summary: One-time 'Early Access' surcharge applied to prorated invoice after plan downgrade
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a one-time line item labeled 'Early Access Surcharge' on the prorated invoice generated immediately after they downgraded from Enterprise Pro -> Enterprise Standard. The surcharge amount (USD 1,250.00) appears to have been applied to the prorated period only; the customer says they did not opt into any early-access program or add-on.

Impact: Customer is disputing the charge and has paused autopay for the invoice. This is blocking renewal and causing accounting review on their side (finance has escalated). Immediate action needed to confirm whether charge is billable or a misapplied tag.

Environment: prod-us-west tenant for org id: stellardocs-prod (customer-facing account). Proration/time window: plan change executed 2026-03-11 18:24 UTC; invoice generated 2026-03-12 02:07 UTC.

Steps to reproduce (as reported):
1) Customer downgraded plan via Console (Enterprise Pro -> Enterprise Standard) on 2026-03-11 18:24 UTC.
2) Billing subsystem calculated prorated credit and generated invoice.
3) Invoice includes normal prorated debit/credit lines and an extra "Early Access Surcharge" (one-off).

Logs/attachments: Customer provided PDF of invoice (attached), Console screenshot showing plan change, and a support log export snippet showing the plan-change event id: EV-20260311-18-24321. Attached to this ticket: invoice_569999_stellardocs.pdf, console-planchange-ev-24321.log.

Requested outcome: Confirm whether the surcharge is legitimate. If incorrect, remove the line, issue a credit memo, and restore autopay. If legitimate, provide clear justification (rate id, policy link, and why it applied during proration).

investigation_notes:
Summary of findings:
- Invoice generation timeline: draft invoice created 2026-03-12 02:07 UTC.
- Tagger service rollout on 2026-03-10 introduced rate_tag 'early_access_beta_v2'.
- Postback reconciler applied a late annotation (2026-03-11 23:59 UTC) which caused a one-off surcharge line to be inserted during finalization.
- The organization stellardocs-prod matched an unintended rollout cohort due to overlapping feature flags (trial_protection + geo_bucket_us_west).
- No sign that customer explicitly purchased or consented to an 'early access' addon.
- Billing policy review: early access surcharge should only apply when customer has 'early_access_optin' meta flag set on subscription; stellardocs subscription does not have that flag.

Hypothesis: A tagging rollout used a faulty cohort expression that matched non-opted-in enterprise tenants. The postback reconciler happily annotated the draft invoice and finalization created the charge.

Data sources checked: invoice line_item table, postback_reconciler logs (recon-id PR-20260311-99), tagger service audit trail, console-plan-change event EV-20260311-18-24321, customer-provided invoice PDF.
resolution_notes:
Action taken so far: 
- Billing Eng rolled back tagger cohort change at 2026-03-13 15:22 UTC (PR revert).
- Engineering created a compensating patch to make the tagger cohort expression stricter; patch merged to canary branch (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/tagger/pull/129).
- Temporary mitigation: placed a hold on collection for invoice INV-20260312-569999 and flagged for manual review in billing dashboard.
- Customer-facing remediation: committed to issue a credit memo for the erroneous surcharge if final verification confirms misapplication.

Next steps and timeline: 
1) Billing team to run reconciliation job to confirm whether early_access line appears on any other finalized invoices for 2026-03-10 -> 2026-03-13 window (ETA 2026-03-13 EOD).
2) If confirmed error, create credit memo and notify customer; expected credit issuance 2026-03-14.
3) Postmortem to be authored if more than 3 customers affected.
4) Improve tagger rollout safety checks (feature flag AND subscription-level optin guard).
